- Le quotidien en version numérique dès 13 heures
Marine Le Pen cible la Ligue des droits de l’homme, un « ramassis de gauchistes »
Visée par Gabriel Attal, la candidate du Rassemblement national appelle à « échapper quelques minutes à la caricature », avant de faire état de 53 milliards d’euros d’argent public versé aux associations chaque année, et, selon elle, de la nécessité de « faire des économies partout. M. Retailleau a raison, il y a un certain nombre d’associations qui, d’année en année, réclament des subventions alors qu’en réalité ils ont des comptes en banque qui grossissent, qui grossissent, qui grossissent. »
« Lesquelles ? », réagissent Gabriel Attal et Raphael Glucksmann. « Je vous donnerai les éléments », balaie Marine Le Pen.
« Des associations communales ou des associations départementales, qui n’ont pas de subventions, mériteraient d’en avoir », poursuit la candidate du Rassemblement national, chiffrant les économies qu’elle entend réaliser à 3,7 milliards d’euros.
« Quelles associations ? », rétorque M. Glucksmann. Puis Gabriel Attal appuie : « Les seules déclarations que vous avez faites, c’est que vous avez dit ce sera les associations qui accompagnent les migrants et des associations [comme la] Ligue des droits de l’homme…. Si vous faites la somme de toutes les associations d’aide aux migrants, d’intégration, la Ligue des droits de l’homme, ça fait 1 milliard d’euros. Où est-ce que vous trouvez les 3 milliards [d’euros] ? »
« M. Attal, nous voulons arrêter de subventionner les associations politisées. J’assume ça. » Interrogée par le journaliste Gilles Bouleau sur la Ligue des droits de l’homme, qui appelle à combattre le Rassemblement national, Marine Le Pen déclare, s’adressant au président de l’association : « Monsieur de la Ligue des droits de l’homme, vous avez parfaitement la possibilité de demander des subventions. Vous n’avez pas la possibilité d’appeler à voter pour untel, (…) d’insulter les candidats ou d’insulter des partis politiques, parce que je considère que l’argent public doit subventionner des associations qui ne sont pas politisées », avant de les qualifier, manifestement agacée, de « ramassis de gauchistes (…) d’une violence à l’égard de la France, d’une violence à l’égard des institutions qui est une véritable honte ».
Les femmes restent les grandes perdantes du système de retraite français
A la suite du témoignage poignant d’Odile, 73 ans, qui gagne environ 1000 euros par mois après avoir élevé seule trois enfants et mené une carrière hachée, plusieurs candidats, comme Gabriel Attal, Bruno Retailleau ou Raphaël Glucksmann, ont pris les femmes en exemple des laissés-pour-compte du système français.
Au niveau national, d’après les derniers chiffres de la direction de la recherche, des études, de l’évaluation et des statistiques (Drees), leurs pensions de droit direct demeurent inférieures à 37 % de celles des hommes (50 % en 2004), et de 25 % en incluant l’éventuelle pension de réversion, dont bénéficient plus souvent les femmes. Une situation qui reflète en partie les inégalités de carrière liées aux enfants.
Plusieurs mesures sont entrées en vigueur au 1er septembre 2026 pour réduire quelque peu ces inégalités, comme un calcul de la retraite désormais basé sur vingt-trois ou vingt-quatre années au lieu de vingt-cinq, ou un accès au départ anticipé pour carrière longue facilité.
Gabriel Attal assure qu’il ne baissera pas les subventions aux associations
« Que faites-vous pour lutter contre la solitude ? », demande la journaliste à Bruno Retailleau qui répond : « Les associations. » « Donc vous faites tout reposer sur les associations », lui répond la journaliste. « Mais le lien, c’est les associations, mais le lien, c’est aussi le travail. J’y reviens parce que le travail ce n’est pas une aliénation, c’est ce qui permet de vivre dignement, ce n’est pas seulement des conditions de subsistance », assure le candidat Les Républicains (LR).
Alors que la parle était donnée à Gabriel Attal, Raphaël Glucksmann et Jean-Luc Mélenchon prennent la parole à sa place. Le candidat Renaissance arrive finalement à prendre la parole après une sorte cacophonie générale. « Ce qui me frappe dans ces débats, c’est qu’on finit par perdre de vue ce qui devrait être notre idéal à tous (…) Notre objectif, ça doit rester qu’à la fin il n’y ait plus besoin des Restos du cœur, ou en tout cas dans des proportions beaucoup moins importantes », assure l’ancien premier ministre sous Emmanuel Macron. Il assure qu’il ne baissera pas les subventions aux associations et qu’il maintiendra le cadre fiscal qui permet d’avoir des déductions fiscales pour soutenir ces dernières.
Alors qu’il cible directement Marine Le Pen en évoquant le cas d’une commune dirigée par le Rassemblement national (RN) où le gaz a été coupé par le maire pour l’association du Secours populaire, on assiste à un rare moment de communion entre plusieurs candidats qui approuvent ses propos.
« Je considère que les associations doivent être apolitiques », assure Marine Le Pen
Selon la candidate Rassemblement national (RN), les associations ne devraient ne pas prendre part aux débats politiques : « Je considère que les associations doivent être apolitiques (…) Si elles veulent faire de la politique, c’est tout à fait leur liberté. Mais à ce moment-là, il faut qu’elles se constituent un parti politique. »
« Si vous êtes au pouvoir, vous allez décider que telle ou elle association est politique », la reprend Raphaël Glucksmann. « Ça veut dire que si vous passez des lois xénophobes et que des associations refusent de les appliquer ou les contestent, vous allez supprimer leurs subventions. Ça donne un pouvoir à l’Etat complètement délirant », s’inquiète l’eurodéputé. « L’accueil universel, c’est le principe de toutes les associations qui font de l’aide sociale », ajoute-t-il.
« C’est vraiment important ce que vous dites, et c’est faux », dit la candidate d’extrême droite. « Moi, je suis dans mon rôle politique. Je présente une vision politique, je fais des choix politiques, et il y a un monde associatif qui n’a pas, lui, précisément à faire de choix politique », reprend de son côté Marine Le Pen.
« Sans ces bénévoles, sans ces travailleurs sociaux, le pays se serait effondré », affirme Raphaël Glucksmann
« Depuis 2024, il y a eu 4 milliards [d’euros] de coups de rabot aux associations », pose le candidat Place publique, avant de brandir la une du Journal du dimanche daté du 20 septembre et titré « 60 milliards engloutis par les associations ». « Il y a eu une campagne idéologique, un combat culturel, un combat politique qui est mené contre les associations (…). Ce genre de titre-là, ce genre de campagne relayée ensuite par les partis politiques qui adoube (…), c’est extrêmement dangereux. »
Puis, il prend la défense des « 12 millions de bénévoles, le million de travailleurs sociaux de ce pays [qui] tiennent la France debout. Sans ces bénévoles, sans ces travailleurs sociaux, le pays aujourd’hui se serait effondré. Effondré parce que quand la puissance publique recule, eh bien, qui prend ? Qui prend la relève ? C’est vous. »
Il a exposé sa mesure d’un cadre pluriannuel sur cinq ans où l’association sait quel est le niveau de la subvention qu’on reçoit sur cinq ans, avant de fustiger « cette bureaucratie permanente où on est obligé de répéter cinq fois les mêmes démarches bureaucratiques quand on est dans une asso[ciation] ». Puis, le candidat a plaidé pour le maintien d’un Fonds social européen, alors qu’un cinquième des repas des Restos sont financés par l’Union européenne, et pour qu’on élève la part de l’aide alimentaire dans ce fonds, de 3 % à 5 %.
« Si demain, les Restos du cœur devaient fermer, vous faites quoi ? », questionne Romain Colucci, bénévole et fils de Coluche
« Le monde du bénévolat va mal. Les bénévoles sont inquiets parce qu’après avoir vu les services publics se rétrécir, ils voient aujourd’hui se rétrécir des associations. Certaines disparaissent. Donc ma question est simple : si demain, pour des raisons économiques, politiques ou sanitaires, les Restos du cœur devaient fermer, vous faites quoi ? », a questionné Romain Colucci, bénévole aux Restos du cœur, pour introduire le thème de la place des associations dans la société française.
Coluche, son père – qui s’était déclaré candidat à la présidentielle de 1981 – et fondateur de l’association, « aurait été satisfait de voir que tous les candidats ont répondu à l’appel des Restos du cœur », s’est-il félicité.
Jean-Luc Mélenchon défend son allocation d’autonomie pour les étudiants
Jean-Luc Mélenchon rappelle qu’il est très compliqué pour les étudiants de cumuler les études et le travail pour payer les études. « J’ai pris un engagement, c’est l’allocation d’autonomie, soit 1 337 euros, c’est au-dessus du seuil de pauvreté », et pour payer cette mesure il propose de saisir l’héritage au-delà de 12 millions d’euros. Le candidat « insoumis » rappelle son attachement à la défense de l’enseignement professionnel et technologique.
Bruno Retailleau répond à Jean-Luc Mélenchon en lui rappelant qu’il existe bien une possibilité où l’on peut travailler et étudier : l’apprentissage. « C’est bon pour le jeune, il a un salaire ; c’est bon pour la famille », dit le candidat LR alors que Jean-Luc Mélenchon à l’air sceptique sur l’utilisation du terme salaire. « C’est un début de salaire », reprend Bruno Retailleau.
Bruno Retailleau plus à la page que Jean-Luc Mélenchon sur le pilotage de l’apprentissage
Les candidats « insoumis » et républicain se sont écharpés sur la question de l’apprentissage, que Bruno Retailleau entend développer. « Mon projet, c’est de confier aux régions l’apprentissage et la formation professionnelle, et vous verrez, ça marchera beaucoup mieux ».
Après avoir rappelé qu’il avait été « ministre de ça » (en l’occurrence, ministre délégué à l’enseignement professionnel, de 2000 à 2002), Jean-Luc Mélenchon l’a sèchement repris : « C’est déjà le cas, monsieur qui vient d’inventer l’eau chaude. Ce sont les régions qui dirigent le plan de développement des formations professionnelles. » « Vous voulez rire, a rebondi M. Retailleau. J’ai été président de région et depuis 2018, les régions, on leur a enlevé justement la compétence de l’apprentissage. »
D’un point de vue juridique, la politique d’accès à la formation professionnelle des jeunes et des adultes est une compétence de la région, mais elle est une compétence de l’Etat pour les jeunes encore sous statut scolaire ou universitaire. La loi de libéralisation de 2018 qu’évoque Bruno Retailleau a toutefois profondément modifié le système de formation professionnelle initiale, en instaurant un nouvel établissement public chargé de la régulation de la formation professionnelle et initiale au niveau national, France Compétences, et en libéralisant l’offre et la demande. Par là même, cette réforme a signé la fin du pouvoir de régulation des régions sur le sujet, devenu véritablement effectif en 2021, après plusieurs années de transition.
Raphaël Glucksmann : « J’ai honte du monde qu’on lègue »
Répondant à Féthia, bénévole et bénéficiaire des Restos du cœur de 25 ans, qui a fait part du nombre important d’étudiants en situation de précarité et a demandé les mesures des candidats « pour que chacun puisse vivre dignement et que les richesses du pays soient mieux réparties entre tous », Raphaël Glucksmann fait part de sa « honte du monde qu’on lègue » aux jeunes, énumérant la « catastrophe climatique, l’explosion des inégalités, la perspective de vivre plus mal que ses parents » ainsi que « l’explosion de la détestation des uns, des autres, du racisme, de la xénophobie dans notre pays, la perspective de la guerre sur notre continent. Mais qui sommes-nous si nous acceptons de léguer un monde comme ça ? »
Pour répondre au premier point – la catastrophe climatique –, le candidat met en avant sa taxation des plus hauts patrimoines. Quant à la mobilité, M. Glucksmann souhaite la mise en place d’un pass mobilité destiné aux moins de 25 ans à 1 euro journalier, avant de souligner une « révolte extrêmement profonde qui a été méprisée par ce gouvernement, qui a été ignorée par ce gouvernement. Et c’était une erreur terrible », faisant allusion au mouvement lycéen et étudiant.
« J’assume ce qui a été réussi » et « j’assume les échecs » dit Gabriel Attal
« J’assume ce que j’ai fait dans les fonctions qui m’ont été confiées au moment où elles m’ont été confiées. J’assume ce qui a été réussi et je l’ai dit tout à l’heure, un taux de chômage au plus bas depuis quarante ans (…) J’assume les échecs. Et, oui, sur la pauvreté, malheureusement, la pauvreté n’a pas reculé », admet Gabriel Attal qui, en tant qu’ancien ministre et premier ministre sous Emmanuel Macron, est régulièrement interpellé par ses concurrents.
Il se dit d’accord avec ce qu’a dit plus tôt Bruno Retailleau sur les inégalités et notamment que pour y remédier il faut aller à la racine de celles-ci à savoir l’école. S’il reconnaît que des économies sont nécessaires au global, Gabriel Attal assure qu’il n’y aura pas d’économie pour l’école.
Gratuité du permis de conduire ; train gratuit aux heures creuses… Les propositions de Marine Le Pen sur la jeunesse
Comment améliorer la vie des étudiants ? C’est la question qui est posée à la candidate d’extrême droite. « D’abord, j’ai envie de vous dire, ça passe par les mesures que j’ai proposées tout à l’heure sur la baisse de la TVA sur l’énergie (…) Il faut la TVA 0 % sur les produits de première nécessité », assure la candidate Rassemblement national (RN). Elle liste alors une série de mesures en faveur de la jeunesse dont une augmentation de leurs revenus en tant qu’apprentis en fonction de leur âge, mais aussi de créer des logements étudiants dont les bureaux vides.
Elle propose également le permis gratuit pour tous les jeunes, peu importe le revenu de leurs parents, sauf pour les étudiants qui ont « un casier judiciaire long comme le bras ». Marine Le Pen se dit aussi en faveur de la gratuité des trains pour les jeunes aux heures creuses.

Grève dans la fonction publique, perturbations dans les transports, manifestations… A quoi s'attendre pour la mobilisation du 17 novembre ?
Les syndicats appellent les agents de la fonction publique, de l'Education nationale ou encore des transports à faire grève mardi. Des dizaines de manifestations sont annoncées, auxquelles doivent se joindre lycéens, étudiants et gilets jaunes.
Nouvelle journée de mobilisation sociale. De nombreux syndicats appellent les agents de la fonction publique à faire grève mardi 17 novembre, notamment pour réclamer une hausse des salaires face à l'inflation.
Des dizaines de manifestations sont prévues dans toute la France, auxquelles doivent également participer des organisations lycéennes et de gilets jaunes qui veulent poursuivre les mouvements entamés en septembre.
Grève dans la fonction publique, l'éducation, la santé et les transports
L'appel à la grève a été lancé le 9 novembre par une intersyndicale de la fonction publique rassemblant la CGT, l'Unsa, la FSU, Solidaires, la CFE-CGC et la Fédération autonome de la fonction publique (FAFP). L'appel a été rejoint par Force ouvrière, et par la branche Fonction publique de la CFDT "faute d'engagement budgétaire clairement assumé par Matignon" en faveur des agents publics.
Les syndicats réclament une "revalorisation immédiate et significative" de "la valeur du point d'indice" des fonctionnaires, qui n'a pas bougé depuis 2023 malgré l'inflation. Le gouvernement a, depuis, annoncé une hausse de 1,6% du Smic au 1er décembre, et une revalorisation des plus bas salaires de la fonction publique, mais ces mesures sont qualifiées de "miettes" par la secrétaire générale de la CGT, Sophie Binet.
Dans les transports, les cheminots sont également appelés à la grève par une intersyndicale composée de la CGT, de la CFDT et de Sud Rail, "dans la continuité du 5 novembre" quand "plus d'un cheminot sur trois" était en grève selon la CGT. "La circulation des trains sera normale pour les TGV INOUI, faiblement à fortement perturbée sur les trains Transilien, RER et les trains régionaux TER", rapporte la SNCF.
Du côté des TER, le trafic sera perturbé en Bourgogne-Franche-Comté, en Bretagne, en Centre Val de Loire, dans les Hauts-de-France, en Nouvelle Aquitaine et en Occitanie. En Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes et dans les Pays de la Loire, le trafic sera perturbé uniquement sur certaines lignes. La circulation sera normale dans le Grand Est, la Normandie et en Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur. En Ile-de-France, le trafic sera perturbé sur le RER D et les lignes de transilien J et R et "légèrement perturbé" sur la ligne N.
Dans le transport maritime, les ports seront aussi touchés par l'appel à la grève de 24 heures lancé par la fédération CGT de ports et docks, "pour les salaires, les pensions et les services publics". La représentativité du syndicat est de 95 % parmi les dockers, qui chargent et déchargent les marchandises, et de 87,5 % parmi l'ensemble des salariés de la manutention portuaire au niveau national.
Côté éducation, le Snes-FSU (premier syndicat des collèges et des lycées généraux et technologiques) et SUD Education appellent donc les personnels du premier et second degré à la grève. Les organisations étudiantes, comme l'Unef, l'Union étudiante ou l'Union syndicale lycéenne, appellent aussi à la mobilisation. Le ministère de l'Education nationale anticipe un taux de grévistes de 3,73% dans le premier degré public, selon un message transmis aux médias lundi en début d'après-midi.
Le 5 novembre, 10,46% des agents de la fonction publique d'Etat avaient fait grève, selon un communiqué du ministère de l'Action et des Comptes publics. Ils étaient 6,10% dans la fonction publique territoriale, et 4,97% dans la fonction publique hospitalière, selon la même source.
De nouvelles manifestations partout en France
A Paris, une manifestation est organisée à l'appel de l'intersyndicale régionale d'Ile-de-France, qui rassemble la CFDT, la CFE-CGC, la CGT, la FSU, FO, Solidaires, l'Unsa, l'Union étudiante, l'Unef, la Fage et l'Union syndicale lycéenne. Elle partira à 14 heures de la place de la Nation, rapporte la CGT et l'Union étudiante. Des mobilisations sont également prévues dans toute la France. La CGT et le Snes-FSU proposent chacun une carte qui recense plusieurs dizaines de rassemblements programmés pour le 17 novembre.
A l'échelle nationale, les manifestations du samedi 14 novembre ont rassemblé 106 000 personnes selon le ministère de l'Intérieur, et 200 000 selon l'intersyndicale jeune citée par Radio France. Les manifestations du 5 novembre avaient rassemblé 575 000 manifestants selon le ministère de l'Intérieur, et près de 1,6 million de personnes selon la CGT.
"Nous serons aux côtés des syndicats le 17 novembre, qui se trouve être également le huitième anniversaire des gilets jaunes", a déclaré sur franceinfo Benjamin Ball, membre de la coordination des gilets jaunes. "Nous appelons à un acte VI samedi" 21 novembre, a-t-il poursuivi. "Les revendications ne sont pas satisfaites, il est normal que nous allions dans la rue de nouveau."

- Une jeune fille de 12 ans interpellée à Paris lors de la mobilisation du 14 novembre et remise à son éducateur de l'Aide sociale à l'enfance par la police
- Manifestations du 14 novembre : un total de 404 personnes interpellées dans toute la France, dont plusieurs dizaines de mineurs

Renault veut aller vite, très vite, partout, tout le temps. Le constructeur automobile français a annoncé, lundi 16 novembre, une vaste réorganisation en France. Un chassé-croisé de 1 090 départs volontaires d’un côté et de 2 000 recrutements de l’autre touchera dix usines en France en plus du centre d’ingénierie de Guyancourt (Yvelines). Ces mesures visent, d’une part, à améliorer « la productivité » des sites, selon le directeur industriel de Renault, Thierry Charvet, et d’autre part à « rééquilibrer les effectifs des ouvriers par rapport aux ingénieurs, qui avaient été beaucoup ajustés » dans le passé, a-t-il reconnu.
Les impacts sociaux seront présentés en comité central d’entreprise dès vendredi 20 novembre puis sur chaque site le 26 novembre, veille du début des négociations sur les conditions du plan de départs volontaires avec les syndicats du groupe, qui devrait ensuite s’ouvrir dès mi-janvier pour se terminer à l’été 2027.
« Renault est bien positionné en termes de qualité et de coûts mais les constructeurs chinois créent des tensions sur les prix », justifie Thierry Charvet. En France, les marques chinoises ont porté leurs parts de marché de 3,4 % en 2025 à 5,2 % en juillet 2026, selon la société de conseil spécialisé sur le secteur automobile Inovev, et le mouvement s’accélère. Elles multiplient les modèles et cassent les prix sur les deux segments stratégiques du constructeur français. D’abord sur celui des petites voitures, son cœur de cible, qui représentent la moitié de ses ventes, et sur lequel Geely et BYD accélèrent avec des petits modèles concurrents de Dacia, la marque low-cost de Renault.

Le ministère public, lors de son réquisitoire jeudi 12 novembre, avait demandé des « peines exemplaires » contre des accusés coupables à ses yeux d’un triple assassinat à la « sauvagerie sans nom », symbolique de l’ultraviolence du narcotrafic marseillais. La cour d’assises spéciale des Bouches-du-Rhône, composée uniquement de magistrats professionnels, a suivi, lundi 16 novembre, après quatre semaines de débats et six heures de délibéré, les demandes des avocats généraux pour les deux principaux accusés de ce procès au long cours.
Karim Harrat, présenté comme le commanditaire des meurtres, et Amine Oualane, un des chefs présumés de la DZ Mafia, son exécutant de terrain « au centre de la bande organisée », sont condamnés à la réclusion criminelle à perpétuité, assortie de vingt-deux années de peine de sûreté pour le premier et de vingt ans pour le second. Un verdict accueilli dans un silence de plomb au sein d’un palais de justice d’Aix-en-Provence (Bouches-du-Rhône) dont le dispositif de sécurité a encore été renforcé dans la perspective de cette ultime journée.

"C'est pire que d'habitude", "Ça va être un bazar"… La fermeture de l'A13 pour neuf mois provoque déjà des bouchons en Île-de-France et inquiète les communes
En semaine
- Présenté par Jean-Baptiste Marteau
- Rédacteurs en chef Elsa-Pallot
- Rédacteurs en chef adjoints Julien Gasparutto, Margaux Manière, Caroline Thébaud
Le week-end
- Présenté par Laurent Delahousse
- Rédacteurs en chef Elsa Pallot
- Rédacteurs en chef adjoints Arnaud Comte, Margaux Manière, Julien Gasparutto
Trouver un autre chemin pour aller travailler, c’est le casse-tête qui commence pour les habitués de l’A13, fermée depuis lundi 16 novembre matin à la sortie de Paris, en direction de la Normandie, jusqu’à fin août 2027. Les bouchons étaient déjà nombreux ce lundi, et les communes voisines veulent éviter de récupérer les voitures dans leurs rues. Certains maires ont même sollicité les applications GPS.
Ce texte correspond à une partie de la retranscription du reportage ci-dessus. Cliquez sur la vidéo pour la regarder dans son intégralité.
L'autoroute A13 n'est officiellement fermée que depuis ce lundi 16 novembre au matin. Mais pour les automobilistes, trouver le bon itinéraire tourne déjà au casse-tête. Quelque 330 kilomètres de bouchons étaient cumulés ce soir en Île-de-France. "Je ne sais même plus par où passer. Là, ça fait deux fois que je suis en train de faire le tour. Il y a des rues qui sont fermées, les panneaux sont très durs à suivre", reconnaît un automobiliste. Un conducteur ajoute : "C'est pire que d'habitude. C'était long, très long." "Je travaille à côté de Boulogne et je mets 20 minutes pour rentrer. Là, le temps est doublé", déplore une troisième.
Une portion de l'autoroute A13, le tunnel de Saint-Cloud, est désormais fermée. Construit il y a près de 100 ans, il voit passer habituellement plus de 80 000 véhicules par jour. Mais son état est jugé préoccupant. Des fissures de près de 40 centimètres nécessitaient une fermeture pour travaux qui va durer neuf mois. Deux itinéraires bis sont proposés, dont l'A14 rendue gratuite du lundi au vendredi.

Un arrêté préfectoral interdit de traverser les communes pour éviter la saturation du réseau secondaire. Ukraine has held new talks with United States and European officials on ending the war with Russia, hours before Kyiv’s mayor reported strikes on two bridges in the capital.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described Monday’s online discussions with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and European representatives as “not easy”. But he said participants had agreed to meet in Berlin with the “Coalition of the Willing”, a group of countries supporting Ukraine, as the US and Europe step up peace talks this week.
“Diplomatic processes are actively underway and we hope that these efforts will not be in vain,” Zelenskyy said in his nightly address.
He also warned that Ukrainian intelligence indicated Russia was preparing major strikes that night and throughout Tuesday.
Later on Monday, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said preliminary reports indicated that the North and South bridges across the Dnipro River had been hit. Air defence units were operating, and Reuters news agency witnesses heard a series of loud explosions.
Ukraine on Monday struck a key bridge and targeted oil refineries in what Russian defence ministry data indicated was the biggest overnight drone attack on Russia since the start of full-scale war in 2022. The Crimea Bridge was again struck overnight, with nearly 200 drones intercepted near Moscow, according to Telegram statements.
US envoy reports progress, warns of difficult choices
Kushner, US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, said Washington was making progress towards an agreement in coordination with Russia, Ukraine and Europe.
“Important challenges remain, and a final agreement will require difficult decisions,” he wrote on X.
He said he and Witkoff had also spoken with Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov about the next steps. Their discussions included how to arrange direct engagement between Europe and Russia so each could hear the other’s concerns and proposals.
The exchanges followed last week’s talks in Abu Dhabi, where US, Ukrainian and Russian officials met together for the first time in nine months. Those negotiations produced an agreement on a prisoner exchange but no breakthrough on ending the war.
Witkoff and Kushner later met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow and said European representatives would join the next round. On Monday, Moscow disputed that assertion.
Europe prepares to join, Moscow withholds agreement
Zelenskyy said representatives from France, Germany, Britain, Italy and Poland had participated fully in Monday’s discussion and would have the same representation in future meetings with Russian negotiators.
Ushakov said Russia had not agreed to expand the talks beyond the existing Russian, Ukrainian and US delegations. No date had been agreed for the next round, he added.
European governments, meanwhile, were preparing their negotiating team while maintaining pressure on Moscow.
Irish Foreign Minister Helen McEntee welcomed renewed talks and the agreement on EU representation following diplomatic meetings in Abu Dhabi and Dublin last week. But she said, “Russia has clearly not changed its position.”
Speaking ahead of Monday’s meeting of EU foreign ministers in Brussels, McEntee said 113 new sanctions on Russia were intended to maintain pressure on Moscow “as it intensified attacks on civilians and critical infrastructure during the winter”.
“We are also working to ensure Ukraine has the finance and the military support it needs while advancing Ukraine’s path to EU membership,” she said.
Russia rules out a temporary respite
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Russia wanted a lasting peace rather than a temporary ceasefire that would allow Ukraine to recover from the damage inflicted by Russian forces.
He said Moscow sought peace lasting “years, even centuries”, adding that negotiations were complex and could take considerable time.
Separately, Trump said he would discuss the war with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Putin in China, saying he believed Putin wanted to end the war.
“I think he’s backing down a little bit,” Trump told reporters. “Frankly, I think he’d like to see it finish.”
The planned Berlin meeting would allow Ukraine and its supporters to agree on their next negotiating steps. Russia had yet to accept their proposed representation in the talks that would follow.

Yemen’s army has said it carried out 661 attacks against Houthi positions across several fronts, killing or wounding 173 fighters, as government forces continue their military campaign amid Houthi territorial gains in the country’s southwest.
Military spokesperson Colonel Majed al-Nuzaili said on Monday that the operations, conducted as part of the ongoing “Dawn of Yemen” offensive, included 15 air strikes, 526 artillery attacks, 53 drone strikes and 67 rocket attacks.
In a statement on X, al-Nuzaili said the attacks had destroyed or damaged 71 military vehicles and pieces of equipment, as well as command-and-control centres, observation posts and fortifications.
He said government forces, backed by the Popular Resistance, were continuing to confront Houthi movements in the provinces of Taiz, Marib and al-Jawf, while operations were also under way on southern fronts.
The military said it would continue its offensive until it achieved its objectives, while taking precautions to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure.
The latest operations followed a series of battlefield setbacks for government-aligned forces, which have withdrawn from strategic positions near the Bab al-Mandeb Strait and are repositioning to defend Aden, the temporary capital of Yemen’s internationally recognised government.
Al Jazeera’s Yousef Mawry reported that the Houthis had cut off a key government supply route along the Red Sea coast, forcing troops to abandon several positions as concerns grew over a possible Houthi offensive towards Aden.
Parliament moves to outlaw Houthis
The military escalation coincided with a political development, as Yemen’s parliament unanimously approved a bill designating the Houthis a “terrorist organisation” and criminalising their activities, financing and supply of weapons.
According to the state-run Saba news agency, the bill provides for prosecuting those involved in violations attributed to the group, freezing and confiscating affiliated assets, and imposing tougher penalties for offences, including attacks on civilians, planting landmines and targeting international shipping.
The legislation will now be submitted to Rashad al-Alimi, chairman of Yemen’s Presidential Leadership Council, for enactment.
The latest developments come six weeks after government forces launched “Dawn of Yemen” on October 5, seeking to regain territory controlled by the Houthis, including the capital, Sanaa.

U.N. talks seek to rein in 'killer robots' as fears over AI weapons grow
GENEVA — Negotiations on possible rules for the use of lethal autonomous weapons, also known as 'killer robots' are underway at the United Nations in Geneva.
Supporters of controls on autonomous weapons say this week's U.N. conference on Certain Conventional Weapons (or CCW), which meets just once every five years, is the last best chance to agree rules before it is too late.
Warfare technology has advanced rapidly in the last few years, with some experts warning that the world is just months away from having weapons that can choose targets and make the decision to kill autonomously.
In Ukraine and Gaza, AI-assisted weapons have already been used to take out targets, with Ukrainian civilians reporting being 'hunted' by drones as they shop or go to school. But these are still controlled remotely by humans.
Humanitarian organizations say the decision to kill – and responsibility for that choice – must stay in human hands. Ahead of this week's meeting, the United Nations, the International Committee of the Red Cross and the Pope have all called for legally binding rules. U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned that allowing fully autonomous weapons to kill would be 'crossing a moral red line'.
What are the risks?
The Red Cross is especially worried that existing rules of war – the Geneva Conventions – cannot be fully respected by autonomous weapons. War is often chaotic and confusing, and the situation can change rapidly. Under the Conventions, soldiers who are wounded or in the process of surrendering can no longer be targeted.
Georgia Haines, a legal adviser with the Red Cross, worries that autonomous weapons will not be able to distinguish between a soldier who is still fighting, one who is wounded and one who wants to surrender.
'The risk is that, based on the technology we are seeing, they are not able to understand in the same way that a human is the contextual signals. And so the risks are incredibly high that there will be a misidentification of a target.'
Meanwhile, human rights groups warn that the technology behind AI-assisted weapons is becoming increasingly cheap and easy to use. The more it is adopted by the military, the greater the danger of proliferation and its use by terrorist groups or law enforcement agencies in repressive regimes. In theory, a swarm of autonomous drones could be programmed to kill everyone wearing a red sweater, everyone carrying a poster or even everyone speaking a certain language.
Many of the countries now meeting in Geneva take such concerns very seriously. At least 50, including Ireland, Italy, Brazil, Mexico, France and Germany, are calling for a strict timetable to agree on binding rules governing autonomous weapons.
But among states that are already developing and using semi-autonomous weapons, there is pushback. The United States, Russia and Israel have indicated they are set to oppose legally binding rules, with Washington proposing a five-year timetable to draft non-binding guidelines instead.
The U.S. is traditionally a late adopter of international treaties. It did not ratify the Ottawa Convention on landmines, for example, although it did, over time, stop deploying them and reduce its stockpiles.
Under President Trump, doubts about international law have grown. Washington has imposed sweeping sanctions on the International Criminal Court, and just this weekend, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in a keynote speech to the Federalist Society, warned against "quoting laws to men with swords."
The problem for states meeting in Geneva is that U.N. negotiations on limiting specific weapons are supposed to be conducted by consensus. This was achieved in 1995, when countries agreed to a ban on blinding lasers, but other agreements have proved elusive. With landmines, countries frustrated by the delay finally took negotiations outside the U.N. process to create the Ottawa Convention.
This week, there may be a compromise: a longer or even open-ended negotiating period to come up with rules that individual states can adopt as binding or non-binding. For diplomats supporting such a solution, it is a way to ensure at least some progress. For campaigners, it is less than ideal, with one likening it to kicking a very dangerous can down the road.

ABSTRACT
Neoclassical demand obeys regularity: adding a good can only draw demand away from existing 
goods. In a natural field experiment with Lyft covering 7.2 million riders and 47 million choices, we 
randomize the presence and price of a premium ride. Contrary to regularity, the premium ride raises 
demand for the cheapest incumbent and for not buying. The effect grows with the premium price 
and with repeated exposure, and persists in sessions where the premium ride is not displayed. 
Rational inference and inattention cannot account for these facts. A model in which a surprisingly 
high price, cued on the app and retrieved from memory, draws attention to prices explains them.

1 Introduction
Deciding which products to offer is key for firms. Airlines carve economy into basic and
premium tiers; smartphone makers add flagships; ride-hailing apps charge extra for a
faster pickup. Such moves shape the menu consumers face. How do they affect choice?
In neoclassical theory a new product allows a firm to better match some consumers’
tastes, drawing demand from the firm’s other products, rivals, and from not buying any-
thing. Consumers gain, and so does the firm if the product is well chosen (Tirole, 1988).
What a new product cannot do is to make any existing option more attractive. For de-
terministic utility this is the Weak Axiom of Revealed Preference (Samuelson, 1938): a
consumer facing a larger menu either switches to the new good or keeps her previous
choice. With random utility, it is the weaker regularity condition: adding an alterna-
tive lowers the choice probability of each incumbent option, the outside option included.
These properties shape the effect of new goods on demand, profits and welfare.
We test them in a natural field experiment with the ride-sharing company Lyft, ran-
domizing 7,242,942 riders across 47,616,543 choice occasions, none of whom knew
they were participating in a study. Control riders chose between “Wait & Save,” cheap
but with a long pickup window, and “Standard,” faster and more expensive. Treated rid-
ers saw the same two products at the same prices, plus a premium option, “Fast Pass,”
faster and more expensive still. We also randomized the Fast Pass price across three lev-
els, always above Standard, holding its pickup time fixed. In the neoclassical model the
vertically superior Fast Pass attracts riders with a high value of time, reducing the share
choosing Standard and possibly also the shares choosing Wait & Save and not buying.
We detect a violation of this prediction taking three forms. First, adding Fast Pass
raises the share of the cheaper Wait & Save option and of not buying (while decreasing
the share of Standard). One interpretation is that Fast Pass raises riders’ price elasticity,
2
moving them toward cheaper options. Second, the effect is stronger for higher Fast Pass
prices, which therefore raise riders’ price elasticity. Third, the effect also grows stronger
over time; Experience with Fast Pass raises price elasticity. Magnitudes are meaningful.
In a rider’s first exposure, demand for Wait & Save rises by about 2 and 3 percent of its
baseline share, while the probability of making no request rises by a more modest 0.3-0.5
percent; across all sessions, the Wait & Save effect is roughly five times larger. The effect
of adding Fast Pass in a given pricing condition on the share of not buying equals that of
a uniform 1.17 percent increase in every Lyft price; the effect of Fast Pass on the share
of Wait & Save equals that of a 1.25 percent decrease in this option’s price.
The violation of regularity shows that, contrary to standard screening logic, the pre-
mium tier did not move riders up the menu: it moved them down. It also differs from
violations of WARP such as the compromise and decoy effects (Simonson, 1989; Huber
et al., 1982), in which adding a premium product should favor more expensive incum-
bents; here it favors the cheaper one and not buying. What causes these effects? One
rational account is information: the menu alters riders’ inference about the firm or sit-
uation (Wernerfelt, 1995; Kamenica, 2008). These models, however, generate the com-
promise effect, not its opposite. We examine other forms of menu-based inference and
argue that they fail too. A chief reason is that rational riders would learn that Fast Pass
and its price are random, and hence uninformative, so the effect should fade over time.
Instead, it grows. Another account is rational inattention: consumers optimally choose
what to learn about their options, so a new good shapes valuation of incumbent goods
(Matˇejka and McKay, 2015). Here Fast Pass should matter especially if it is worth learn-
ing about, so the violation of regularity should shrink when Fast Pass is more pricey and
hence chosen less often. In the data the effect is largest at the highest price, where Fast
Pass is chosen by only one percent of riders.
3
We show that the data can be explained by a model of salience where, following Bor-
dalo et al. (2020, 2026), current cues and past experiences prompt a rider to represent
choice as a “large price variation” situation, increasing her bottom-up attention to prices
(K˝oszegi and Szeidl, 2013; Bordalo et al., 2013). The model produces our three find-
ings. First, upon seeing the expensive Fast Pass, the rider recalls expensive rides from
the past, which increase her perceived price variation. She thus pays more attention to
price, increasing her price elasticity. Second, the effect is stronger when Fast Pass is more
expensive, increasing price elasticity compared to a lower Fast Pass price. Third, experi-
ence with Fast Pass fills memory with high prices, causing perceived price variation and
price elasticity to grow over time.
We also exploit the fact that in some treated sessions Fast Pass was not available due
to limited supply. Even in these sessions, riders treated with high Fast Pass prices exhibit
a higher price elasticity than those treated with low ones. Salience can produce this fact:
the former riders recall higher price variation and thus exhibit higher price elasticity than
the latter riders. Consistent with memory, this effect is however weaker than the effect
detected when Fast Pass is available.
We contribute to work on violations of revealed preference (e.g., Simonson and Tver-
sky, 1992; Tversky and Simonson, 1993; Huber et al., 1982; Herne, 1999; Kroll and Vogt,
2012; Crosetto and Gaudeul, 2016; Andreoni and Miller, 2002; Somerville, 2022). Much
of it relies on laboratory experiments, leaving open whether violations survive in real
markets, where experience and self-selection can attenuate anomalies (e.g., List, 2003;
Enke et al., 2023; Rodemeier, 2025; Miller et al., 2026). Two natural field experiments
add a premium option in an online bookstore (Gu et al., 2018) and recommend it on a
travel aggregator (Rafai et al., 2022); the first finds a compromise effect, the second no
effect.1 We present a large-scale natural field experiment that randomizes the presence of

over time. We find an anti-compromise effect: the premium good raises price elasticity,
sorting consumers into the cheaper option and into not buying, the more so the higher its
price and the longer the exposure. Our findings relate to Gennaioli et al. (2026). Their
field violation of revealed preference can also be explained by their treatment (nonlinear
vs linear pricing) increasing price salience and elasticity.

2.1 Design and Sample
The experiment ran from November 5, 2020 to January 20, 2021. Randomization was at

2.5 Mechanisms
The observed failure of regularity is inconsistent with neoclassical stable tastes. It sug-
gests that Fast Pass may increase riders’ price elasticity, promoting the cheaper W&S and

2) Why does it get stronger with repeated exposure to Fast Pass? and 3) why should ex-
posure to higher Fast Pass prices promote W&S and not buying even if Fast Pass is not
available? We discuss theories of context effects and their consistency with our findings.

4 Conclusion
In a natural field experiment with 7.2 million riders we show that adding a premium prod-
uct violates regularity, the weakest implication of stable tastes. Contrary to compromise
and decoy effects, the premium option pushes riders toward the cheapest option and out
of the market. The effect grows with the premium price and with exposure, and survives
in sessions where the premium option is absent. These patterns defy rational inference
and inattention, and are produced by a model where a striking price, cued on the screen
or retrieved from memory, raises attention to prices bottom up.
Three implications follow. First, a firm widening the range of prices on display can
make consumers price-conscious rather quality-focused, so that the direct demand for
the new product is partly offset by higher price sensitivity. The effect is not small. At
the high Fast Pass price, Table 2 shows that for every 100 treated sessions Fast Pass
gains 1.1 riders, while 0.3 stop buying. Since an upgrade earns only the markup while a
lost ride costs the whole fare, the lost rides alone wipe out a Fast Pass markup around a
quarter of the fare. The 1.3 riders downgrading from Standard to W&S add to the loss.

of 72 percent, as observed. The same ρ implies all-sessions effects relative to control of 0.4 and 0.7 p.p.
at the medium and high price, against 1.1 and 1.3 observed. The conclusion is unchanged with a finite
number of sessions per rider.
21
Second, demand estimation imposing regularity can be problematic: in our experiment, a
“regular” demand model would impose that Fast Pass boosts demand for Lyft, attributing
the increased shares of W&S and not buying to a negative taste shock. It would thus
measure the benefit of Fast Pass from upgrades but miss entirely its price-sensitivity
cost. Third, and finally, our findings show the importance of formalizing the cognitive
drivers of context effects: they can allow to unveil the conditions in which compromise
or anti-compromise effects can arise and the amplification of effects through exposure
and cues. Accounting for cognition can help recover hedonics and optimal pricing from
observed demand, as in Gennaioli et al. (2026).

Abstract
Background
Height is a key marker of early-life nutrition and health. China’s four-decade food transition provides an opportunity to examine associations between food consumption and child/adolescent height. We aimed to identify food consumption patterns associated with greater height and favorable sustainability profiles and develop a score quantifying food–height associations.
Methods and findings
We conducted an observational study using height data from ~1.7 million Chinese students aged 7–18 years in the Chinese National Survey on Students’ Constitution and Health (1985–2019) and provincial food consumption data from the National Bureau of Statistics (1985–2023). Temporal trends were examined across three socioeconomic transition phases (1985–1999, 2000–2010, and 2011–2023). Elastic net regression, weighted quantile sum regression, and principal component analysis were used to identify food groups and consumption patterns associated with height, followed by assessments of environmental and economic profiles. Associations were adjusted for provincial socioeconomic and environmental factors, including per capita gross domestic product, educational attainment, sunshine duration, and temperature. A Food Consumption–Height (FCH) score was developed using machine-learning models and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP)-derived food-group weights to quantify each food consumption associated with height and preliminarily validated in an independent observational sample from Guangzhou. From the 1980s to the 2020s, China’s food consumption became more diverse alongside increasing height. Eggs and seafood showed stable associations with height across periods, while milk and fruits became increasingly important after 2000. Nine food consumption patterns were identified across the three periods. A pattern characterized by higher consumption of fruits, nuts, eggs, and milk (FUEL) showed the strongest and most consistent association with greater height in the most recent period (ρ = 0.518, 95% CI [0.453, 0.580]; p < 0.001) and was linked to lower environmental and economic burdens. Height-associated food consumption patterns generally exhibited more favorable nutritional profiles, particularly higher calcium density and calcium-to-phosphorus ratios. Further nutrient-level analyses showed positive associations of protein, calcium, and zinc densities with height and an inverse association for carbohydrate density across all three periods. The FCH score was positively associated with height (β = 0.075, 95% CI [0.069, 0.082]; p < 0.001), and this association showed preliminary consistency in 3,917 participants aged 10–16 years from the Guangzhou Student Nutrition and Health Survey. The main limitations of this study are the observational design and reliance on population-level food consumption data, which limit causal inference between dietary patterns and height outcomes.
Conclusions
The FUEL food consumption pattern was associated with greater height in children and adolescents while placing relatively low environmental and economic demands. The nutrient findings suggest nutritional quality, beyond total energy supply, may help explain the observed food–height associations. The FCH score provides a data-driven score to quantify the association between food consumption and growth outcomes at the population-level. These findings offer evidence to inform food system and nutrition strategies that aim to promote healthy growth within sustainable limits.
Author summary
Why was this study done?
- Over the past four decades, China has experienced major changes in food consumption, alongside substantial increases in height among children and adolescents.
- Which long-term food consumption patterns are associated with greater height and lower environmental and economic burdens remains unclear.
- No simple score is available to quantify the relationship between food consumption and height in children and adolescents.
What did the researchers do and find?
- We examined long-term changes in food consumption and height using data from ~1.7 million Chinese students aged 7–18 years and provincial food consumption data from 1985 to 2023.
- We identified a food consumption pattern characterized by higher consumption of fruits, nuts, eggs, and milk, termed the FUEL pattern; populations following this pattern had greater height and showed relatively favorable environmental and economic profiles.
- We further developed a Food Consumption–Height (FCH) score and found in preliminary validation among 3,917 children and adolescents that higher scores tended to be associated with greater height.
What do these findings mean?
- Food consumption patterns associated with greater height in children and adolescents can be compatible with relatively favorable environmental and economic profiles.
- The FCH score may provide a simple, data-driven tool for future studies to quantify and compare the relationship between food consumption patterns and growth outcomes.
- The main limitations of the study are that the main analyses used population-level food consumption data and the validation was observational. Further longitudinal studies and randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm these findings.

Introduction
Achieving healthy growth while ensuring sustainable nutrition remains one of the most pressing challenges in the global food system. Height is a well-established biomarker of early-life nutrition and health [1]. Within the normal range, taller stature has been associated with lower risks of cardiovascular disease and all-cause mortality [2], as well as higher income and socioeconomic status [3]. However, these relationships are not necessarily linear, and extreme stature may also be linked to specific health risks. Human height is influenced by multiple factors, including genetics, nutrition, and environmental factors [4]. Among these, adequate and diverse nutrition is essential for achieving optimal growth potential. Childhood and adolescence are critical periods of growth, accounting for ~20% of adult height attainment [5]. The current record-high global adolescent population is growing up amid rapid urbanization, climate change, widening socioeconomic inequalities, and a global dietary shift toward high-calorie but low-nutrient patterns [6,7], all of which may profoundly affect physical development and long-term health. Addressing these challenges requires identifying dietary strategies that support healthy growth while promoting environmental sustainability.
China, with its vast territory and diverse dietary cultures, provides an empirical setting for examining how food consumption associations between physical growth and developmental health [8]. Over the past several decades, the average height of Chinese children and adolescents has increased substantially [1]. Between 1985 and 2019, Chinese nineteen-year-old males experienced the largest height increase among nearly 200 countries and regions, gaining almost 9 cm, while females ranked third [4]. Despite this progress, many children and adolescents worldwide still fall short of their full height potential. These improvements have occurred alongside substantial changes in food consumption patterns [9]. However, the specific dietary configurations that have supported these improvements in physical development remain poorly understood.
Understanding how changes in food consumption patterns relate to human growth outcomes and sustainability metrics is central to informing equitable nutrition transitions. Previous research has primarily focused on isolated nutrients or short-term associations [10,11], overlooking long-term, system-level transformations. Integrating large-scale temporal datasets with individual-level records provides an opportunity to quantify how diet diversification is associated with human development trajectories across different stages of modernization.
This study analyzed food consumption and height data from 30 provincial-level administrative regions in China from 1985 to 2023. We identified stable food groups and food consumption patterns linked to height growth across different periods and examined their correlations with height outcomes. We also assessed the environmental and economic performance of these patterns to identify food consumption patterns that were both sustainable and associated with greater height. Building on these findings, we developed a “Food Consumption–Height (FCH)” score to capture the strength of the association between food consumption and height growth, and tested its applicability in a real-world population. We hypothesized that long-term food consumption patterns characterized by nutritionally diverse foods would be associated with greater height growth among Chinese children and adolescents, while also demonstrating favorable environmental and economic profiles.
Methods
Reporting guidelines and analysis plan
This observational study is reported as per the STROBE-nut guideline (S1 Checklist), and the development and evaluation of the FCH score are reported as per the TRIPOD+AI guideline (S2 Checklist). The main analyses were initially planned in June 2025. No prospective study protocol or written statistical analysis plan was prepared for this secondary analysis, and the study was not registered.
During peer review, additional analyses were conducted in response to reviewers’ comments, including alternative principal component analysis (PCA) rotation methods to assess pattern robustness; expanded nutrient profiling and additional nutrient–height association analyses to clarify the nutritional implications of the findings; 1-, 3-, and 5-year lagged analyses to assess temporal robustness; and nutrient intake comparisons across FCH score quartiles in the Guangzhou validation population to evaluate the nutritional relevance of the FCH score.
Ethics statement
The Chinese National Survey on Students’ Constitution and Health (CNSSCH) was approved by the Medical Research Ethics Committee of Peking University Health Science Center (IRB00001052-19095). In accordance with CNSSCH procedures, school principals determined whether written or verbal consent was obtained. Informed consent was obtained from participating children and their parents or legal guardians before data collection. All participant data were anonymized prior to analysis. The Guangzhou Student Nutrition and Health Survey (2023–2024) was approved by the Ethics Review Committee of Guangzhou Center for Disease Control and Prevention (GZCDC-ECHR-2022P0038). Written informed consent was obtained from parents or legal guardians before data collection. No additional ethics approval or informed consent was required for the present secondary analyses, as the analyses were conducted using previously collected data under the relevant ethical approvals and consent procedures.
Data collection
Height z-score.
Height data were obtained from the Chinese National Survey on Students’ Constitution and Health (CNSSCH), a nationally representative quinquennial cross-sectional survey initiated in 1985, with the most recent survey conducted in 2019. The survey included Han Chinese students aged 7–18 years with complete height data from 30 provincial-level administrative regions in mainland China, excluding Tibet, Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan. The CNSSCH applies a multistage, stratified, cluster-sampling design (S1 Methods and S1 Fig). Provincial coverage varied across survey years: Hainan and Chongqing were not included in 1985, and Qinghai and Chongqing were not included in 1995. The sample sizes for 1985, 1995, 2000, 2005, 2010, 2014, and 2019 were 407,692, 204,393, 214,003, 231,898, 215,280, 214,954, and 209,939, respectively (S1 Table). Height-for-age z-scores were calculated using the World Health Organization 2007 growth reference for children and adolescents aged 5–19 years [12], which provides age- and sex-specific standards. These z-scores enabled standardized comparisons of height across survey years and provinces.
Food consumption.
Food consumption data for 31 provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities (excluding Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan) from 1985 to 2023 were obtained from the official website of the National Bureau of Statistics of China. Derived from the annual Urban and Rural Household Survey, these data represent provincial-level per capita household food consumption and reflect population-level food availability rather than individual dietary intake among children and adolescents (S2 Methods). Because food categories were refined over time, some food groups, including beans, milk, fruits, and nuts, were not reported separately before 2000. These values were therefore treated as unavailable rather than as zero consumption.
Validation data.
Data for FCH score validation were obtained from the Guangzhou Student Nutrition and Health Survey (2023–2024). This repeated cross-sectional study, initiated in 2011, was conducted across eight districts in Guangzhou and involved questionnaire surveys of elementary, junior high, and high school students (S3 Methods).
Temporal trends in food consumption and height growth
We used the linear trend test or the Jonckheere–Terpstra test to examine the temporal trends of height z-scores and food consumption across different years.
Identification of food consumption patterns
The periodization of national food consumption patterns (1985–2023) was determined by comprehensively considering multiple factors, including (1) data coverage across survey years in the China Statistical Yearbook, (2) the breakpoints identified via Joinpoint regression analysis, and (3) historical context in China’s economic development and food availability. Based on these criteria, the study period was divided into three distinct phases.
PCA was used to identify food consumption patterns within each period. Suitability for factor analysis was assessed using the Kaiser–Meyer–Olkin index and Bartlett’s test of sphericity [13]. PCA with varimax orthogonal rotation was performed [14] to improve interpretability, and robustness was evaluated using alternative rotation methods, including quartimax, promax, and oblimin rotations, while keeping food variables, analytic sample, and number of retained components unchanged. Components were retained based on eigenvalues > 1, scree plot inflection points, and cumulative variance explained [15]. Foods with rotated factor loadings >0.60 were considered representative of a pattern. The total principal component scores for each consumption pattern were calculated using standardized food consumption values and factor score coefficients. Additional details are provided in S4 Methods.
Nutrient profiling and nutrients-height associations
To better interpret the associations between food consumption patterns and height, we estimated province-level nutrient supply from reported food consumption data. Broad food categories were disaggregated into specific food items using the FAO Food Balance Sheets (FBS), and nutrient contents and edible portions were assigned using the Chinese Food Composition Tables (S2 Table). Nutrient supply and nutritional quality indicators were compared across transition periods and food consumption patterns using Kruskal–Wallis tests with Dunn–adjusted pairwise comparisons. Additional methodological details are provided in S5 Methods.
We further examined the associations of total energy and key nutrients, including protein, fat, carbohydrate, calcium, and zinc, with height z-score and absolute height using multivariable linear regression models separately for 1985–1999, 2000–2010, and 2011–2019. Except for total energy, nutrients were expressed as nutrient density per 1,000 kcal to reduce the influence of differences in total energy intake and better reflect food composition. Models were adjusted for the same covariates as in the primary analyses. Effect estimates were reported per 1-SD increase in each exposure.
Single, combined, and pattern-level food-height associations
We used nationwide province-level data to assess the associations between major food consumption and height z-scores among children and adolescents across the three periods. To contextualize the findings, China’s annual gross national income per capita was benchmarked against the World Bank’s yearly income classification thresholds based on the Atlas method. The classification broadly aligned with the three study periods: China was predominantly low income before 1999, lower-middle income from 1999 to 2009, and upper-middle income from 2010 to 2023 [16] (S3 Table).
Pearson correlation coefficients were computed to explore the linear associations between food consumption (kg/year) and height z-scores. To identify the food groups most strongly associated with height z-scores while accounting for multicollinearity, we employed elastic net regression [17], with optimal α and λ parameters selected through cross-validation. To improve estimate stability, 1,000 bootstrap resamples were used to estimate 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and foods were ranked according to the magnitude of their coefficients (S6 Methods).
Key food groups identified from these analyses were further evaluated using weighted quantile sum regression [18] to assess their joint associations with height z-scores. Within each period, food combinations were defined as pairwise, three-way, and higher-order combinations of these key food groups.
All models were adjusted for annual mean sunshine duration, annual mean temperature, provincial-level educational attainment (proportion of the population with at least high school education), and provincial GDP per capita. For each combination, 100 bootstrap iterations were performed to estimate effect sizes with 95% CIs, and combinations were ranked according to the magnitude of their associations.
Partial correlation analyses were conducted to examine the associations between food consumption pattern scores and height z-scores, adjusting for provincial GDP per capita, annual mean sunshine duration, annual mean temperature, and provincial-level educational attainment. The 95% CIs were estimated using 2,000 bootstrap resamples. In addition, given the cumulative nature of height linear growth and the absence of a clearly established optimal exposure window, we conducted 1-, 3-, and 5-year [19,20] lagged sensitivity analyses at both the key-food and food consumption-pattern levels to assess the temporal robustness of these associations. Because height measurements were available at 5-year intervals, height outcomes for some lagged years were estimated by linear interpolation. Covariates were aligned to the corresponding exposure year, and analyses were performed for both height z-score and absolute height.
Estimation of environmental impact and economic burden for food consumption patterns
Environmental burden was defined as the estimated environmental footprint associated with each food consumption pattern, and assessed using greenhouse gas emissions, land use, freshwater withdrawals, acidification, and eutrophication. Environmental and economic indicators for specific food groups were obtained from the global database developed by J. Poore and T. Nemecek [21] (S6 Table), which quantifies environmental impacts for 40 food types worldwide. To better characterize food composition within the broader food categories reported in the China Statistical Yearbook, we integrated food composition data from the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) FBS.

Development and preliminary observational validation of the FCH score
To systematically evaluate the ability of various food consumption items to predict height and their marginal contributions, we trained multiple machine-learning models and evaluated their predictive performance using food consumption data as predictors and absolute height (cm) as the continuous outcome. The specific models included random forest, XGBoost, generalized linear model, K-nearest neighbors, elastic Net, Partial Least Squares, and gradient boosting machine. Data were randomly split into training and testing sets in a 7:3 ratio. Ten-fold cross-validation was performed within the 70% training set for model development, parameter tuning, and model performance assessment. After hyperparameter tuning and model selection, the final model was evaluated on the held-out 30% test set for internal evaluation. The FCH score was subsequently evaluated in an independent observational sample from the Guangzhou Student Nutrition and Health Survey. Model performance was assessed using Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and coefficient of determination (R2), and the model with the best overall performance was selected [22]. Model implementation and hyperparameter settings, together with the procedures for sensitivity analysis and uncertainty estimation, are described in S8 Methods. We assessed sensitivity to hyperparameter choices by varying one parameter at a time and quantified uncertainty in test-set RMSE, MAE, and R2 using 2,000 bootstrap resamples of the fixed test-set observed–predicted pairs. The results are presented in S10 Table.
After selecting the best-performing model, Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis was applied to quantify the marginal contribution of each food group to height prediction [23]. SHAP analysis was performed on observations from both the training and test sets. Dependence plots were generated to visualize nonlinear relationships and potential interactions among variables. The FCH score weights were derived from the SHAP analysis. Specifically, for each food group, the magnitude of its weight was determined by its mean absolute SHAP value across all observations, which reflects its average contribution to height prediction in the selected model. Because mean absolute SHAP values indicate the strength, but not direction, of the association, the sign of each weight was assigned based on the overall relationship observed in the SHAP dependence plots. Food groups for which higher consumption was associated with higher SHAP values were assigned positive weights, whereas those for which higher consumption was associated with lower SHAP values were assigned negative weights. Results
Temporal trends in food consumption and height growth
From the 1980s to the 2020s, food consumption patterns among Chinese residents became increasingly diverse. Analysis of 14 food groups in the China Statistical Yearbook showed rising consumption of seafood, animal and vegetable oils, beef and mutton, poultry, eggs, pork, nuts, fruits, beans and milk, while consumption of grains, vegetables and mushrooms, and sugar declined (p for trend < 0.001, Fig 1a and S1 Table).

Over the same period, Chinese adolescents grew taller. The mean height z-score of Han students aged 7–18 years increased, from –1.1 ± 0.9 in 1985 to –0.5 ± 1.0 in 2000, and 0.1 ± 1.0 in 2019 (p for trend < 0.001; Fig 1a and S1 Table). The greatest increases occurred in northeastern and eastern China, which had the highest height z-scores by 2019 (Fig 1b), whereas Guangdong, a southern province, showed the smallest improvement (S2 and S3 Figs). Similar increasing temporal trends were observed when absolute height was used (S4 Fig).
Temporal progression of single and combined food-height associations
The population-level associations between specific food groups and height z-scores remained largely stable over time. Based on food classification differences and Joinpoint regression, the study period was divided into three phases: 1985–1999, 2000–2010, and 2011 onward (S5 Fig). The 2000 breakpoint mainly reflected changes in food-category reporting in the China Statistical Yearbook, as several food groups, including beans, milk, fruits, and nuts, were not separately reported before 2000. The 2011 breakpoint was identified by Joinpoint regression and was interpreted in relation to China’s post-2010 socioeconomic transition [24] and continued changes in food availability and consumption structure [25].
Across all periods, eggs and seafood consistently showed the strongest associations with height z-score (Figs 2a and S6). In 1985–1999, eggs (r = 0.62, p < 0.001), seafood (r = 0.37, p = 0.010), and vegetable oil (r = 0.44, p = 0.002) were the top positive correlates and key contributors in elastic net models. In 2000–2010, eggs (β = 0.15, 95% CI [0.02, 0.26]), seafood (β = 0.05, 95% CI [0.00, 0.14]), and milk (β = 0.07, 95% CI [0.00, 0.16]) became major positive contributors. By 2011–2019, a wide range of foods, including grains, beans, seafood, eggs, milk, and fruits, showed positive associations with height. Across the 1-, 3-, and 5-year lag periods, eggs and seafood remained consistently positively associated with height, consistent with the contemporaneous analyses (S8 and S9 Tables).

Food combinations including eggs and seafood showed the largest association estimates with height z-scores (Fig 2b). In 1985–1999, their combined consumption showed the strongest association with height z-score (β = 0.15, 95% CI [0.14, 0.15]). During 2000–2010, the combinations seafood + eggs and seafood + eggs + milk showed the largest effects (β = 0.20, 95% CI [0.19, 0.21]). By 2011–2019, the key combination expanded to “grains + seafood + eggs”, with similar associations observed when milk or fruits were included. Sensitivity analyses using measured average height produced consistent findings (S7 Fig).
Evolution of food consumption patterns
The Kaiser–Meyer–Olkin indices for food consumption data (0.673, 0.824, and 0.717 for 1985–1999, 2000–2010, and 2011–2023) and significant Bartlett’s test (p < 0.001) confirmed the suitability of factor analysis; three principal components were retained in each period (S8 Fig).
Overall, Chinese food consumption evolved from a simple, carbohydrate-based structure to a more balanced and diverse pattern (Fig 3a). From 1985 to 1999, three dominant patterns were identified: high Vegetable oil–eggs (VIE) pattern, high Poultry–seafood–sugar (PEA) pattern, and high Vegetables and mushrooms (VM) pattern. During 2000–2010, the VIE pattern transitioned to Fruits–nuts–milk–eggs–vegetable oil (FUME) pattern; the PEA pattern became Poultry–pork–seafood (PKS) pattern, and a new Beef and mutton–sugar (BUS) pattern appeared. By 2011–2023, the FUME pattern further evolved into the Fruits–nuts–eggs–milk (FUEL) pattern, while the PKS pattern evolved to Pork–poultry–seafood (PLS) pattern with increased pork consumption, and BUS pattern remained largely unchanged. Advantages of the FUEL pattern
The FUEL pattern was associated with better height outcomes and greater sustainability. From 2011 to 2023, the population following this pattern had the highest mean height and height z-scores (ANOVA and Tukey HSD, both p < 0.001, Fig 3b). Its predecessor, the FUME pattern, showed similar benefits from 2000 to 2010.
After adjustment for provincial GDP per capita, annual mean sunshine duration, annual mean temperature, and provincial-level educational attainment, the associations between principal component scores and height z-scores remained pattern-specific (Fig 4a). During 1985–1999, the PEA pattern showed the strongest positive association with height z-scores (partial ρ = 0.763, 95% CI [0.727, 0.794]; p < 0.001), followed by the VIE pattern (partial ρ = 0.474, 95% CI [0.405, 0.538]; p < 0.001). During 2000–2010, the FUME pattern showed the strongest positive association (partial ρ = 0.765, 95% CI [0.730, 0.794]; p < 0.001), followed by the PKS pattern (partial ρ = 0.309, 95% CI [0.231, 0.384]; p < 0.001). During 2011–2023, the FUEL pattern remained positively associated with height z-scores after adjustment (partial ρ = 0.518, 95% CI [0.453, 0.580]; p < 0.001), meanwhile the PLS pattern showed a weak positive association (partial ρ = 0.089, 95% CI [0.008, 0.170]; p = 0.031). Sensitivity analyses using measured average height produced similar results (S9 Fig). Lagged sensitivity analyses further supported the temporal robustness of these associations (S10–S15 Figs). Across the 1-, 3-, and 5-year lag periods, the VIE and PEA patterns during 1985–1999, the FUME and PKS patterns during 2000–2010, and the FUEL pattern during 2011–2019 remained positively associated with height outcomes. The VM pattern during 1985–1999 and the BUS pattern during 2000–2010 remained not significantly associated with height outcomes, whereas the PLS pattern during 2011–2019 was no longer significantly associated with height outcomes in the lagged analyses. These findings were consistent for both height Z-score and absolute height.

C’est une belle victoire pour l’écosystème du logiciel libre en France : lors de la transposition de la directive européenne NIS 2, l’Assemblée nationale supprime une disposition qui menaçait directement les éditeurs de logiciels. Explications.
Lors de la reprise des débats parlementaires le lundi 9 novembre 2026 autour du projet de loi relatif à la résilience des infrastructures critiques et au renforcement de la cybersécurité, les députés ont corrigé une dérive législative qui inquiétait vivement les défenseurs du numérique ouvert. Dans un communiqué publié à l’issue du vote, l’association April salue le retrait d’une disposition ajoutée en commission qui assimilait sans distinction tous les éditeurs de logiciels à des « entités essentielles ».
Une surtransposition qui menaçait les acteurs du logiciel libre
L’alerte remontait à septembre 2025, lorsque la commission spéciale chargée d’examiner ce texte de transposition avait modifié l’article 8 pour y inscrire la catégorie générique des « éditeurs de logiciels », sans même en préciser les contours juridiques. Une telle qualification aurait soumis de nombreuses structures, y compris des acteurs modestes ou des mainteneurs de briques open source, à un régime de conformité et de contrôle taillé pour les opérateurs d’infrastructures vitales. Dès l’adoption de cette version en commission, l’April avait appelé à la vigilance face aux conséquences opérationnelles d’un tel flou.
Cette extension allait bien au-delà du périmètre prévu par Bruxelles et créait un doublon manifeste avec le règlement européen sur la cyberrésilience (Cyber Resilience Act), texte spécifiquement conçu pour encadrer la sécurité des produits comportant des éléments numériques et tenir compte des spécificités des modèles collaboratifs libres.
Cinq amendements adoptés avec l’aval du gouvernement
Lors de la séance publique du 9 novembre 2026 — dont les débats sont consultables en vidéo à partir de la minute 36:30 sur le portail de l’Assemblée nationale —, plusieurs députés de différents groupes politiques ont défendu la suppression de cette mention jugée contre-productive. Les amendements 135, 188, 197, 213 et 311 ont tous été adoptés, bénéficiant à la fois de l’avis favorable du rapporteur du texte et du soutien du gouvernement.
En écartant cette surtransposition française, le législateur préserve la compétitivité des éditeurs français et évite d’asphyxier l’écosystème du logiciel libre sous des contraintes administratives inadaptées, tout en maintenant l’exigence de sécurité attendue des véritables infrastructures critiques du pays.
